title: Plant nuclei extraction protocol for single nuclei RNA-seq
author: Bruno Guillotin

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Enzymatic Pre-digestion
steps.instruction: Perform optional enzymatic pre-digestion to soften cell walls, noting that this may induce transcriptional changes.

substeps.instruction: Place fresh sample (e.g., root tips cut to 3-4 mm or leaves cut into ~1mm pieces) in a 30mm diameter Petri dish with ≈1ml enzyme solution and start timer.
Place in a vacuum chamber for 1min, break vacuum, and vacuum for another 1min.
Incubate at room temperature on a horizontal agitator at 90 rpm for ≈20mins (adjust based on sample: Nodules 30mins, Roots 10-15mins, leaves ~20mins).
Transfer samples into a cell strainer by pouring the solution or using tweezers.
Place the cell strainer on towel paper to remove most of the enzyme.
Transfer the cell strainer into a new 30mm Petri dish containing 2ml post-enzyme washing buffer and agitate.
Place the cell strainer on towel paper again to remove more enzyme.
Transfer the cell strainer into another new 30mm Petri dish containing 2ml post-enzyme washing buffer and agitate.
Place the cell strainer on towel paper and use a small spatula to transfer the sample into 300ul of nuclei lysis buffer on ice.

steps.title: Mechanical Nuclei Extraction
steps.instruction: Mechanically lyse the cells to release nuclei while keeping samples chilled.

substeps.instruction: For roots, transfer into a pre-chilled 60mm plastic petri dish on ice with 300ul lysis buffer and chop using 2 razor blades for at least 5mins until no large pieces remain.
Transfer samples using a P1000 into a pre-chilled 1.5ml Eppendorf tube with a pre-chilled blue plastic pestle (if material is low, wash the petri dish with 100ul lysis buffer and transfer).
Perform 20 up-down movements with twisting using the blue pestle to grind samples.
Incubate on ice for 2–3mins to finish cell lysis, then perform 10 more movements with the pestle.

steps.title: Initial Filtration and Washing
steps.instruction: Filter the lysate and perform the first round of centrifugation and washing.

substeps.instruction: Filter samples through a 20um strainer (CellTrics, 04-0042-2315) into a pre-chilled 1.5ml Eppendorf, using 200ul lysis buffer to wash remaining tissue from the filter.
Centrifuge samples at 4°C for 10 mins in a bucket centrifuge at 500g (maize) or 1000g (Arabidopsis).
Remove supernatant without disrupting the pellet, leaving only a few ul.
Add 500ul washing buffer and gently resuspend nuclei with a P1000 until no clumps are visible.

steps.title: Secondary Washing and Final Resuspension
steps.instruction: Perform a second wash and resuspend nuclei in the final buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge samples at 4°C for 5 mins in a bucket centrifuge at 500g (maize) or 1000g (Arabidopsis).
Remove supernatant without disrupting the pellet, leaving only a few ul.
Add 50ul of Final buffer (Note: if using 10X genomics multiome kit, use the provided multiome nuclei buffer instead of Final Buffer) and resuspend by flicking or gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Final Filtration
steps.instruction: Perform a final fine filtration to remove remaining debris.

substeps.instruction: Filter the sample through a 10um strainer (PluriSelect 43-10010-50) into a fresh pre-chilled 1.5ml Eppendorf, applying pressure with a thumb on top of the filter.
If material is low, wash the tube and filter with an additional 10ul of Final buffer.

steps.title: Nuclei Counting and Concentration Adjustment
steps.instruction: Quantify nuclei using a hemocytometer and adjust the concentration.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DAPI working solution: 1) 10mg/mL stock in mmq water; 2) 1ul stock 1 in 499ul mmq water; 3) 1ul stock 2 in 99ul mmq water; 4) Add 1ul stock 3 to 9ul purified nuclei.
Load 9ul of final volume onto a 0.1mm Hemocytometer with a normal coverslip (not the provided thick one).
Using a fluorescent microscope at 63x, focus on a red square in bright field, then switch to DAPI filter and fluorescence.
Count only well-rounded nuclei within the square border, adjusting the z-axis to capture all nuclei.
Repeat for 6 to 8 random squares.
Calculate concentration: (Average nuclei per square) * 16 * 10 * dilution = nuclei per ul of final buffer.
Adjust concentration to 2,000–4,000 nuclei per ul by diluting or concentrating via centrifugation (500g for 3mins and removing supernatant).

steps.title: 10X Genomics Loading
steps.instruction: Add the adjusted nuclei to the 10X master mix immediately before loading.

substeps.instruction: Add the appropriate amount of nuclei (do not exceed 15ul of nuclei buffer) to the 10X master mix at the last minute.
Mix gently by pipetting and load into the 10x Chromium controller.

steps.title: Optional Additional Purification
steps.instruction: Use these strategies if the sample contains excessive debris or chloroplasts.

substeps.instruction: Strategy 1: At steps 17 and 20, centrifuge for 3min at 50g to pellet debris, transfer supernatant (leaving 50ul) to a new tube, then proceed with the original step.
Strategy 2: Resuspend pellet in 200ul washing buffer. Slowly layer this on top of 500ul cushion buffer (1.7M sucrose instead of 0.3M) in a 1.5ml Eppendorf.
Centrifuge for 5min at 4°C at 1000g.
Remove supernatant (containing chloroplasts) and proceed to step 19 or 22.

steps.title: Fixation Reagent Preparation
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the lyophilized fixation reagent in a chemical fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL DMSO to one Fixation Reagent tube.
Vortex at high speed repeatedly until all white solids are fully dissolved.

steps.title: Sample Fixation Procedure
steps.instruction: Fix the nuclei for small samples and perform subsequent washes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fixation mix: 222 µL Methanol, 5.5 µL reconstituted Fixation Reagent, and 2.2 µL DEPC. Vortex and keep on ice.
Rapidly add 200 µL of the Complete Fixation Solution to the 1.5-mL tube containing resuspended nuclei in 50 µL Final Buffer; pipette strongly up and down four times.
Incubate on ice for 15 minutes, inverting the tube every 5 minutes (white precipitate is normal).
Add 500 µL scale Wash Buffer and resuspend by flicking until precipitate disappears.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 5 min at 500–1000g (Maize–Arabidopsis); optionally increase time to 8–10 min or increase speed for better recovery.
Remove supernatant, leaving ~30 µL residual volume.
Add 250 µL scale Wash Buffer and resuspend by flicking.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 5 minutes at 500–1000g (Maize–Arabidopsis).
Remove supernatant, leaving ~20–30 µL residual volume; resuspend by flicking.
Take 2–5 µL in a 0.2-ml PCR tube for counting and freeze the remainder at −80°C.
